earth.name: Earth
earth.tagline: The cradle of humanity — and the perfect place to return to.
earth.description: Earth remains the most habitable world in the known solar system, with a breathable nitrogen-oxygen atmosphere, liquid water oceans, and a magnetic field that shields surface life from solar radiation. Whether you're departing or arriving, orbital approach offers unrivalled views of swirling cloud systems and turquoise seas.

hazards.item0: Dense air traffic in low-Earth orbit — strict approach corridors enforced
hazards.item1: Electromagnetic interference from surface networks may disrupt navigation
hazards.item2: Weather re-entry delays are common at equatorial spaceports
hazards.item3: Customs and biosecurity screening required for all interplanetary arrivals

mars.name: Mars
mars.tagline: Rust-red horizons and the promise of a second home.
mars.description: Mars is humanity's boldest frontier — a terrestrial planet with a thin carbon dioxide atmosphere, polar ice caps, and the largest volcano in the solar system. Olympus Base offers pressurised habitats, rover excursions across Valles Marineris, and spectacular iron-oxide sunsets.

hazards.item0: Dust storms can ground all surface operations for weeks
hazards.item1: EVA suit required at all times outside pressurised zones
hazards.item2: Radiation exposure ~2× Earth levels — shielding mandatory
hazards.item3: Gravity adjustment syndrome affects most travellers for 48–72 h
hazards.item4: Perchlorate soil contamination — never remove gloves outdoors

item2.description: North polar CO₂ ice cap, summer

moon.name: Moon
moon.tagline: Humanity's first step — now a bustling gateway world.
moon.description: Just 384,000 km from Earth, the Moon is the solar system's most accessible off-world destination. Lunar Gateway Station and Artemis Base Camp provide modern amenities, while the stark regolith plains and Earth-rise views make for an unforgettable experience.

hazards.item0: No atmosphere — space suit required outside at all times
hazards.item1: Micro-meteorite impacts are a persistent risk in the regolith zone
hazards.item2: Temperature swings exceed 300 °C between day and night
hazards.item3: Abrasive lunar dust can damage seals and optical surfaces

item0.description: Earthrise over the Sea of Tranquility

venus.name: Venus
venus.tagline: Hellscape below, paradise above the clouds.
venus.description: Venus is the solar system's most extreme planet — crushing atmospheric pressure, sulphuric acid clouds, and surface temperatures hot enough to melt lead. Galaxium's Cloud City habitats float at 50 km altitude where temperature and pressure are surprisingly Earth-like, offering surreal amber skies and lightning storms below.

facts.atmosphere: CO₂ 96 %, H₂SO₄ clouds — lethal at surface

hazards.item0: Surface descent is strictly prohibited — habitat stays airborne
hazards.item1: Sulphuric acid rain can dissolve exposed equipment within hours
hazards.item2: Atmospheric turbulence rating 9/10 — expect a rough arrival
hazards.item3: Pressurisation failure evacuation time: under 90 seconds
hazards.item4: All exterior maintenance requires level-4 acid-resistant suits

item0.description: Aerostat Cloud City at 50 km altitude

item2.description: Solar array wings above the cloud deck

jupiter.name: Jupiter
jupiter.tagline: King of planets — come for the storms, stay for the scale.
jupiter.description: Jupiter's swirling bands of ammonia and hydrogen stretch across a disc 11 times wider than Earth. Galileo Station orbits above the Great Red Spot, offering research suites, observation decks, and the most dramatic sky-scape in the solar system. Not for the faint-hearted.

facts.atmosphere: H₂ 90 %, He 10 % — immense pressure at depth

hazards.item0: Radiation belts around Jupiter are among the most intense in the solar system
hazards.item1: Magnetic field disrupts electronics — shielded hull required
hazards.item2: No solid surface — descent below cloud tops is a one-way journey
hazards.item3: Orbital insertion requires precise timing to avoid moon conjunctions
hazards.item4: Gravitational tidal stresses can cause hull fatigue on long stays

item0.description: Great Red Spot storm system, 350-year duration

item2.description: Io transit shadow across the equatorial band

europa.name: Europa
europa.tagline: Beneath the ice: the best chance of alien life in our solar system.
europa.description: Europa's fractured ice shell hides a vast subsurface ocean that may harbour microbial life. Research Station Icebreaker sits at the surface, while deep-drilling missions descend toward the water below. Every visit contributes to one of the most exciting scientific endeavours in human history.

hazards.item0: Jupiter's radiation at Europa's orbit is intense — exterior exposure is time-limited to 1 hour
hazards.item1: Ice crust seismic "ice-quakes" can crack landing pad anchorings
hazards.item2: Cryoventing plumes erupt unpredictably — avoid surface EVA near fracture lines
hazards.item3: All samples require level-5 biosafety protocols — no surface material leaves containment

item2.description: Jupiter rising over Europa's ice plain

pluto.name: Pluto
pluto.tagline: The edge of the known — for travellers who want more.
pluto.description: Pluto sits at the outer frontier of our solar system, a nitrogen-ice world with heart-shaped plains, soaring methane mountains, and a hazy blue atmosphere. Sputnik Base is the most remote inhabited outpost in human history, and arrival is a rite of passage for serious space explorers.

facts.atmosphere: N₂, CH₄, CO — thin and seasonal

hazards.item0: Extreme cold requires next-generation cryo-insulated EVA suits
hazards.item1: Low gravity increases fall risk — standard locomotion training required
hazards.item2: Communication lag to Earth exceeds 4 hours — emergency response is self-reliant
hazards.item3: Nitrogen geysers can emerge without warning near Tombaugh Regio
hazards.item4: Methane frost on landing pads creates slippery surfaces — approach speed limits enforced

item0.description: Tombaugh Regio nitrogen ice plains ("The Heart")

item2.description: Blue haze layers in Pluto's thin atmosphere
